paper_b.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow

metadata.description: Two near-simultaneous formulations of continuous-time generative modeling as regression of a neural velocity field on conditional/expected velocities along an interpolation between noise and data. Lipman et al. derive Conditional Flow Matching from a probability-path / push-forward / continuity-equation viewpoint with a general Gaussian-path family that includes a straight-line OT instance. Liu, Gong, Liu derive Rectified Flow from a transport-coupling / expected-velocity viewpoint and additionally introduce reflow to drive trajectories toward straightness. Core objects (interpolation, regression target, marginal-preserving property, training/sampling algorithm) coincide; framings, motivations and the straightening / reflow analysis differ. This is parallel rediscovery (PR).

matches.explanation: Both papers state the same goal of learning a deterministic transport from a simple prior $\pi_0$ (or $p_0$) to a data distribution $\pi_1$ (or $q$) via simulation-free training of a neural velocity field. Lipman frames it as 'simulation-free CNF training' (push prior to target through a learned ODE), Liu frames it as a 'transport mapping' / coupling problem. Same problem, slightly different vocabulary (CNF vs. transport map).

Lipman's 'time-dependent vector field' $v_t(x)$ together with the 'marginal vector field' $u_t(x) = \int u_t(x|x_1) \frac{p_t(x|x_1)q(x_1)}{p_t(x)} dx_1$ serves the same role as Liu's 'expected velocity' $v^{\mathbf{X}}(x,t) = \mathbb{E}[\dot X_t \mid X_t = x]$. Both are the conditional expectation of an instantaneous velocity given the current state; Lipman defines it via a marginalization integral over $x_1$, Liu defines it directly as a conditional expectation, but for the linear interpolation $X_t = tX_1+(1-t)X_0$ they coincide.

Lipman's 'flow' (diffeomorphism solving the ODE $\dot\phi_t = v_t(\phi_t)$) and 'continuous normalizing flow' map to Liu's 'rectifiable process / rectified flow' $Z_t = Z_0 + \int_0^t v^{\mathbf{X}}(Z_s,s)ds$. Both objects are the integral curve of a (learned) velocity field; Liu emphasizes the rectifiability / uniqueness condition, Lipman uses standard ODE existence as part of the CNF setup.

Lipman's 'conditional probability path' $p_t(x|x_1)$ (and its specialization to a Gaussian conditional path) has no direct counterpart in Rectified Flow. Liu does not condition on data $X_1$ to define a path; instead the path is defined by the joint linear interpolation of a coupling $(X_0,X_1)$. Liu's nonlinear extension (EP233.5) uses generic interpolations $X_t$ but never names a 'conditional probability path'.

Lipman's 'marginal probability path' $p_t(x) = \int p_t(x|x_1)q(x_1)dx_1$ is a paper-original construct without a direct named counterpart in Rectified Flow. Liu's law $\mathrm{law}(X_t)$ of the linear interpolation plays a similar role implicitly but is never given an explicit mixture decomposition; the conceptual marginalization is absent.

The push-forward operator $[\phi_t]_* p_0$ and the explicit Jacobian formula are central to Lipman's CNF framing; Liu does not use push-forward notation. Closest analog is the implicit fact that the rectified flow pushes $\pi_0$ to $\pi_1$, but it is stated as $\mathrm{law}(Z_t)=\mathrm{law}(X_t)$ rather than via a push-forward formula.

Both papers cite/use the continuity equation $\dot p_t + \mathrm{div}(p_t v_t)=0$ as the necessary-and-sufficient condition for a velocity field to generate a density path. Lipman tags it as external (Villani 2009); Liu uses it implicitly in the proof of Theorem TP233.1 (PSP233.2). Same external mathematical fact; emitted as 'exact' even though Liu does not extract it as a node.

Lipman's 'OT displacement interpolant' and the OT conditional flow $\psi_t(x)=(1-(1-\sigma_{\min})t)x+tx_1$ describe a straight-line interpolation between a Gaussian prior and a data point, with constant-direction velocity field. Liu's 'straight flow' DP233.5 ($Z_t = tZ_1+(1-t)Z_0$) is exactly the same straight-line interpolation, but defined at the joint coupling level rather than the conditional-Gaussian level. The trajectories and constant velocity $v=Z_1-Z_0$ coincide.

Both are the (intractable, in Lipman's case) regression objective of a neural velocity onto the marginal/expected velocity. Lipman: $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{FM}} = \mathbb{E}_{t,p_t(x)}\|v_t(x)-u_t(x)\|^2$. Liu: $\min_v \int_0^1 \mathbb{E}\|(X_1-X_0) - v(X_t,t)\|^2 dt$, with $X_t=tX_1+(1-t)X_0$. For Liu's linear interpolation, the Bayes-optimal regressor is $v^X(x,t)=\mathbb{E}[X_1-X_0|X_t=x]$ (his EP233.2), playing the same role as Lipman's $u_t$. The two objectives differ in form (Lipman targets the marginal velocity $u_t$ explicitly, Liu targets the regression residual $X_1-X_0$), but both have the same minimizer; relation is analogous, not literally identical.

The Conditional Flow Matching loss $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{CFM}} = \mathbb{E}_{t,q(x_1),p_t(x|x_1)}\|v_t(x)-u_t(x|x_1)\|^2$ becomes, for Lipman's OT/linear path with $\sigma_{\min}\to 0$, $\mathbb{E}\|v_t(\psi_t(x_0)) - (x_1-x_0)\|^2$. This is precisely Liu's Rectified Flow objective EP233.1. Up to the choice of conditional path, the two objectives are the same regression problem with the same target; we mark this 'exact' for the OT-path special case (which Lipman highlights as his preferred instance).

Lipman's OT-CFM closed-form loss $\mathbb{E}\|v_t(\psi_t(x_0))-(x_1-(1-\sigma_{\min})x_0)\|^2$ reduces to $\mathbb{E}\|v_t(tx_1+(1-t)x_0)-(x_1-x_0)\|^2$ as $\sigma_{\min}\to 0$, which is identical to Liu's rectflow objective EP233.1. Same loss function up to an $\epsilon$-regularization on the data endpoint.

Liu's explicit identification of the optimal velocity as a conditional expectation $v^X(x,t)=\mathbb{E}[X_1-X_0|X_t=x]$ is a paper-original identity. Lipman implicitly uses the same fact in deriving the FM=CFM equivalence (TP232.2), but never writes the optimal $v_t$ as a conditional expectation in this closed form.

Liu's closed-form $v^X$ via conditional density and the Nadaraya-Watson kernel estimator are paper-original tools for the low-dimensional / non-parametric setting. Lipman has no analog: he relies entirely on neural-network parameterization and never derives a closed-form integral expression for the optimal $u_t$ over a sample-based estimator.

Liu's nonlinear rectified flow objective $\min_v \int_0^1\mathbb{E}[w_t\|v(X_t,t)-\dot X_t\|^2]dt$ for general time-differentiable interpolations is the abstraction that allows him to subsume PF-ODE / DDIM. Lipman's Conditional Flow Matching (EP232.3) is structurally similar (a regression on a conditional VF target along a conditional path), but the framing as a unification with diffusion is Liu's original; we emit it as 'none' on Liu's side since CFM's match is already covered by EP233.1.

Both theorems state the marginal-preserving property: a velocity field constructed from per-data-point (or per-coupling) targets generates a density path with the correct marginals. Lipman: posterior-weighted average $u_t$ generates $p_t = \int p_t(\cdot|x_1)q(x_1)dx_1$ via the continuity equation. Liu: the rectified flow $Z_t$ has the same marginal law as $X_t$ at every $t$. Both prove via the continuity equation; they are the same conceptual result, framed at different levels (Lipman over conditional paths, Liu over a coupling's interpolation).

Both proofs verify the continuity equation by exchanging differentiation and integration (or by invoking ODE / continuity-equation uniqueness) to show the constructed velocity field generates the target marginal. Lipman's version is a one-line mixture-of-conditionals computation; Liu's invokes uniqueness of the continuity equation (Kurtz 2011, Ambrosio 2008) in addition. Step decompositions PSP232.1-3 and PSP233.1-3 are structurally parallel (differentiate marginal -> apply continuity equation -> conclude).

Composite Level-2 alignment of the proof-step DAGs of TP232.1's proof and TP233.1's proof. Both decompose into: (i) compute $\frac{d}{dt}p_t$ via differentiation under the integral / via the expected velocity; (ii) recognize the continuity equation; (iii) conclude marginal equality. Steps differ in detail but match step-for-step at the meta-level.

The 'FM=CFM gradients coincide' theorem is unique to Lipman: it justifies replacing the intractable marginal-target loss with the tractable per-conditional-path loss. Liu has no analog because his linear-interpolation objective directly regresses on $X_1-X_0$ (a per-sample quantity) and never introduces a separate intractable 'marginal' loss to compare with.
Proof of TP232.2 (FM=CFM gradient identity) has no Rectified Flow analog; see TP232.2 entry.

Lipman's closed-form vector field for an affine-Gaussian flow $u_t(x|x_1) = \frac{\sigma'_t}{\sigma_t}(x-\mu_t)+\mu'_t$ is specific to the conditional-Gaussian-path family. Liu does not parameterize his interpolation by Gaussian conditional paths; he uses the linear coupling interpolation $X_t = tX_1+(1-t)X_0$ directly, so this closed form has no counterpart.
Proof of TP232.3 (Gaussian VF closed form) has no Rectified Flow analog.

Lipman's time-reversal lemma ($\tilde u_t = -u_{1-t}$ generates the time-reversed path) is paper-original and supports the proposition that conditional VFs match the Probability Flow ODE. Liu's framework allows trivial time reversal of the linear interpolation by symmetry, but he does not extract a separate lemma.
Proof of LP232.1 has no counterpart on Liu's side.

Both papers prove that diffusion-based generative models (Score SDE / Probability Flow ODE / DDIM) can be re-cast as instances of their unified flow framework. Lipman shows the conditional VFs from his Theorem 3 (for VE / VP Gaussian paths) coincide with the Song et al. 2020 PF-ODE vector field. Liu shows the PF-ODE training objective is equivalent to his nonlinear rectified flow objective with $X_t=\alpha_t X_1+\beta_t \xi$. Same target result (subsumption of PF-ODE), proved by similar parameter-matching algebra.

Lipman's proposition that the OT conditional flow $\psi_t(x)=(1-(1-\sigma_{\min})t)x+tx_1$ is the OT displacement map between Gaussians is an external/cited fact (McCann 1997). Liu's discussion of optimal couplings (TP233.5, TP233.6) is more general (any convex cost, any 1D pair); the specific Gaussian-Gaussian OT identification is not made on his side.

Both algorithms describe the main training loop: SGD on a least-squares regression of a neural velocity field $v_\theta(x,t)$ onto a per-sample velocity target along an interpolation between $x_0$ and $x_1$. Lipman's Algorithm samples $t,x_1,x$ and regresses $v_t$ onto $u_t(x|x_1)$ (which for the OT path equals $x_1-(1-\sigma_{\min})x_0$); Liu's Algorithm 1 samples $t,(x_0,x_1)$ and regresses $v_\theta$ onto $x_1-x_0$. Same algorithm; the only difference is Lipman's optional $\sigma_{\min}$ regularization on the data endpoint.

Composite L2 alignment of the inner training loops: both decompose into (i) initialize / sample a triple $(t,x_0,x_1)$, (ii) compute the regression target (Lipman: $u_t(x|x_1)$; Liu: $x_1-x_0$), (iii) compute squared loss and SGD step. Lipman extracts four steps including an explicit Adam-loop step; Liu collapses initialization+update into a single 'minimize least-squares' step. Modulo extraction granularity, the inner loops are identical.

Lipman's CNF sampling algorithm (draw $x_0\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)$, integrate the trained $v_t$ ODE on $[0,1]$ with dopri5/midpoint) is exactly the sampling stage of Liu's rectflow Algorithm 1 (Euler / RK45 ODE integration). The 'analogous' tag reflects different extraction granularity (Lipman makes sampling its own algorithm, Liu folds it into rectflow as ASP233.3).

Composite L2 alignment of the sampling step DAGs: (i) draw $x_0\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)$ (or $Z_0\sim\pi_0$), (ii) integrate the trained ODE forward to $t=1$, (iii) return $x_1$. Same three atomic steps in both papers.

Hutchinson trace estimator for CNF log-likelihood is an external (FFJORD) technique used by Lipman to evaluate NLL of the trained CNF. Liu does not report likelihoods and does not invoke the Hutchinson trick.

Both papers cite the same external diffusion baselines: Score Matching (Song et al. 2020) and DDPM (Ho et al. 2020) / Probability Flow ODE / DDIM. These are external-origin nodes; the match is informational and does not influence the pair-level relation classification.

Liu's 'Reflow' algorithm (recursively re-couple via $\mathrm{rectify}$) is a key paper-original contribution that has no direct analog in Lipman. Lipman's framework is one-shot: once the conditional velocity field is regressed, training is done. Liu's iterative straightening loop ($\mathbf{Z}^{k+1}=\mathrm{rectflow}((Z_0^k,Z_1^k))$) is the mechanism by which his method ultimately reduces NFE to one.

Liu's distillation algorithm (train one-step network $\hat T(z_0)=z_0+v(z_0,0)$ to predict $Z_1^k$) is a separate paper-original step downstream of rectflow + reflow. Lipman has no one-step distillation procedure.
Non-parametric Nadaraya-Watson velocity estimator is unique to Liu. Lipman never considers a non-parametric estimator; the entire framework is parametric / neural.

Liu's 'straight (fully rectified) coupling', 'straightness functional' $S(\mathbf{Z})$, and 'non-intersection functional' $V$ are paper-original definitions that drive the convergence theory of reflow (TP233.3, TP233.4). Lipman does not introduce any analogous notion of straightness as a quantitative target; his OT path happens to be straight but no convergence-rate theorem on straightening is given.

Liu's 'rectifiable / rectified coupling' definition and the '$c$-optimal coupling' definition are central to his convex-cost-reduction and straightening analysis. Lipman has no notion of recoupling and does not study transport-cost optimality of his learned flow.

Theorem TP233.2 (rectified coupling reduces every convex transport cost) and its proof are paper-original to Liu and have no Lipman counterpart. Lipman has no statement comparing transport costs of $(X_0,X_1)$ vs.\ $(Z_0,Z_1)$.

Theorem TP233.3 (four equivalent characterizations of straight couplings) and proof are unique to Liu. Lipman never treats straightness as a property to be characterized; OT-path is straight by construction in his case.
$\mathcal{O}(1/K)$ convergence of straightness under reflow is the central convergence-rate result of Liu and has no analog in Lipman.
$c$-optimality $\Rightarrow$ straightness is paper-original to Liu; no counterpart in Lipman.
1D existence/uniqueness of the straight coupling, and the supporting lemma equating straightness with the deterministic monotonic coupling, are unique to Liu. Lipman has no 1D structural result.

Liu's inviscid Burgers' equation $\partial_t v + (\partial_z v)v = 0$ for straight flows is a paper-original observation linking straightness to a classical PDE. Lipman has no analogous PDE characterization.

Liu's VP/sub-VP coefficient parameterization is an external citation (Song et al. 2020) used in his comparison with PF-ODE; Lipman cites the same Song et al. 2020 work but does not extract these coefficients as a node. Cross-paper match is informational only.
